static_traits.name: Chen Sha
static_traits.family_status: Valuing family relationships, having a supportive family
static_traits.social_status: Interpersonal relationships are overall positive, but subjectively feeling 'hard to be truly appreciated'
static_traits.medical_history: No significant past medical history; no previous psychotherapy experience
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, able to self-reflect; humble tone, slightly nervous at the opening but highly cooperative; able to identify and describe emotions and automatic thoughts, tends to downplay their own achievements

basic_info.main_problem: I feel people think I am smart only because I read a lot of books, and anyone could read like me, which makes me feel not truly appreciated and lacking recognition.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of not being appreciated are affecting my self-worth and confidence, so I sought counseling; I hope to continue exploring these feelings and learn to change my views and see myself from different perspectives.

core_beliefs: Others' approval does not equal truly seeing me

special_situations.event: When others praise her as 'very smart/reads a lot'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others praise me only because I read a lot, it means I am not truly outstanding; accepting compliments would seem immodest
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: On the spot, downplays or denies their own strengths, emphasizes 'this is nothing, everyone can do it', and avoids continuing the discussion
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not understand me; this is not worth praising

special_situations.event: When, in social settings, others introduce or evaluate them as 'a person who reads a lot / therefore very smart'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others only see that I read a lot, it means I have no value in other respects and I am ordinary
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing self-presentation, avoiding talking about one's other strengths or uniqueness
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They only see the surface and will not see the real me

special_situations.event: After reviewing one's own achievements or receiving positive feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: To stay humble, one should not take one's own achievements seriously
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Only focusing on shortcomings and parts that can be improved, automatically negating positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These achievements have no value and do not represent my ability

special_situations.event: When invited in counseling to view reading habits as a unique strength
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I admit this is a strength, I will seem arrogant or insincere
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses vague and weakened expressions (such as 'maybe' 'a bit forced') to reduce the intensity of self-affirmation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Saying this would be insincere; it would make me seem boastful

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be truly seen and affirmed
core_conflict.fear: Fears that expressing pride or accepting praise will be seen as arrogant and immodest, leading to being negated or to damaged relationships
defense_goal: Ensuring safety and acceptance in relationships by staying humble and downplaying oneself
Avoiding directly showing the need to be seen and appreciated

object_relations.object_representation: Others who only see the surface and cannot truly understand me
object_relations.linking_affect: Feeling ignored, lost, and looked down upon

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others affirm her strengths and suggest viewing reading as a strength
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes affirmation does not represent understanding of the 'true self', and accepting praise would appear immodest
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm, objective tone, emphasizes 'it is just that I read a lot', using facts and commonality to downplay personal value, avoiding directly expressing the desire to be seen and affirmed.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to express pride or directly affirm oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If expressing pride will be evaluated as boasting, thus being belittled or alienated
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses words such as 'just / however / actually' to shrink achievements, emphasizes that others can also do it, or changes the topic to avoid going deeper.

manifestations: Feeling 'they do not really understand me'
For a long time, feeling not truly appreciated
outcomes: Experiencing neglect and alienation in the relationship

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Internal rule is 'should be humble, do not seek others' recognition'
When receiving compliments, automatically downplays oneself and disqualifies positive feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Accepts others' affirmation cautiously, frequently negating the self with 'I am just ordinary, nothing special'
Appears reserved when discussing own strengths, using weakening expressions such as 'possibly / maybe / a bit forced'

positive_force: Having a supportive family and good social support
Having self-reflection and insight ability, able to recognize negative automatic thoughts
Willing to try new perspectives and exercises, with good motivation
Stable reading habits and learning ability, can be transformed into visible strengths
negative_force: Persistent tendency toward 'negating the positive' and 'mental filtering', finding it hard to accept positive feedback
An introjected rule overemphasizing humility; avoids being recognized
Self-worth is influenced by others' evaluations, worrying about being seen as boastful (external validation orientation)
Automatically devalues achievements, lowering self-efficacy and confidence
When praised, tends to avoid or tone down self-presentation

target_behavior.behavior: When praised by others or when reading habits are mentioned, immediately devalues and negates own achievements and avoids accepting affirmation
antecedent: Others' praise of one's reading habits or cleverness
Topics concerning personal achievements or strengths
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized humility rules (not seeking recognition), the core belief 'I have no special value', and worry that 'accepting praise would seem boastful or insincere'
target_behavior.function: Avoids the discomfort of being evaluated as arrogant or insincere, maintaining a humble self-image
target_behavior.consequence: Sense of self-worth is weakened, confidence declines, and the feeling of 'not being truly appreciated' is continually experienced
